subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record terminate the session, with reconnect recovery required, or should the client discard that record and remain connected?
rationale: Both choices bound memory, but they have different compatibility and availability effects that protocol tests cannot resolve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep Disconnect With Recovery
options.body: Retain strict fail-closed rejection, but require real proof that the channel detects the close and reconnects with bounded backoff.

options.title: Discard Oversized Record
options.body: Enter a bounded discard state until the record terminator, report the protocol violation, and continue processing later legal lines.

options.title: Accept Strict Outage Risk
options.body: Land the current behavior knowing one malformed record may leave the IRC channel disconnected until an external restart.

recommendation.title: Keep Disconnect With Recovery
recommendation.body: Retain strict fail-closed rejection, but require real proof that the channel detects the close and reconnects with bounded backoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent IRC merge and review history makes this person the strongest available owner for the transport lifecycle and compatibility choice.
